sections.h2: Which Falmouth offices deal with tax on a Pendleton County house?
sections.html:
Seller paperwork runs through three counters. The sheriff mails and collects the bill. The Property Valuation Administrator (PVA) sets the parcel value. The county clerk records the deed and keeps any bill that turns delinquent. The county's web page links out to the PVA's own site for values and exemption forms.

  • Sheriff: 202 Chapel Street, Falmouth; tax questions to 859-654-4511.
  • County Clerk: Room 1, 233 Main Street (mail to P.O. Box 112, Falmouth 41040); 859-654-3380. The doors open 8:30 to 4:00 on weekdays and 8:30 to noon on the second and last Saturday each month, holiday weekends excepted.
  • Planning and Zoning: covers Falmouth plus the unincorporated county, with floodplain management, addressing, code enforcement and development review.

The sheriff mails statements to owners only, never to lenders. A seller who pays through escrow should ask the servicer whether the bill arrived.

sections.h2: What dates and amounts apply to the 2026 Pendleton tax bill?
sections.html:
Statements went out September 30, 2026, in plain envelopes with blue lettering reading "2026 Pendleton County Tax Statement." An owner with no bill by October 12 is asked to call. The counter accepts cash, checks, and debit or credit cards (card users pay a convenience fee, and American Express is refused).

What the Pendleton County Sheriff charges for 2026 taxes, shown on a sample $1,000 bill

The sample column is worked out from the sheriff's percentages. The office closes for county and state holidays and the weekends beside them, among them Veterans Day, Thanksgiving week, Christmas week, New Year's, Martin Luther King Day and the afternoon of Good Friday. A video-monitored drop box sits at the front door. Checks left there need the stub from the top of the bill and a daytime phone number, and anyone wanting a receipt adds a stamped return envelope. Cash does not belong in the box.

sections.h2: How do appeals and the homestead exemption work in Pendleton County?
sections.html:
An owner who disagrees with a value sees the PVA or a deputy first, then files with the clerk by the workday after the public roll inspection ends. The roll opens the first Monday in May for thirteen days. Documents decide the hearing, so bring insurance policies, building costs and comparable listings.

The homestead exemption helps owners aged 65 or more and those classed as totally disabled. It removes $49,100 of assessed value for the 2025 and 2026 years. Against the Census median owner-occupied value of $159,800, that leaves $110,700 to be taxed. The PVA takes the application.

sections.h2: What happens to unpaid Pendleton County tax when the house sells?
sections.html:
The lien stays with the land for up to eleven years under KRS 134.015(5), so the title search at closing shows it and the payoff comes from the seller's side of the settlement.

After April 15 the sheriff turns unpaid bills over to the clerk. Interest of one percent a month starts then, with a 10 percent clerk charge and 20 percent attorney charge stacked on. The clerk's website links to a list of advertised delinquent bills. A seller who is behind should get a written payoff figure from the clerk before signing a contract, because a certificate bought by an outside investor carries extra fees and means paying that investor instead.

sections.h2: What will the seller pay the Pendleton County Clerk at closing?
sections.html:
The grantor pays Kentucky's transfer tax, fifty cents per $500 of declared value (KRS 142.050). The clerk takes it before recording. At the $159,800 Census median, the value rounds up to 320 units, so the tax is $160.00.

  • Recording a deed costs $50.00, plus $3.00 for each page after the fifth.
  • Recording a mortgage costs $80.00, and a release of mortgage costs $46.00.
  • Each deed carries a sworn consideration statement from both sides and an address for the following tax bill (KRS 382.135).
  • Transfers between spouses and foreclosure deeds are among the exemptions.

The clerk's posted schedule says prices can vary slightly, so call 859-654-3380 for an exact total before the closing date.

sections.h2: How did Pendleton County take shape, and why does it matter to a seller?
sections.html:
The legislature carved Pendleton County from Campbell and Bracken counties in 1798 and named it for Edmund Pendleton of Virginia. Falmouth began as a settlement called Forks of Licking around 1776, was chartered in 1793, and got one of Kentucky's first sawmills that same year. The county courthouse dates to 1848. Butler appeared around 1852 when the Kentucky Central Railroad came through, and it incorporated in 1868 with a name honoring a congressman from the area.

Today the county covers about 280 square miles, with the Ohio River along the northeast edge. Falmouth sits where the Main and South Licking rivers meet, and Butler lies ten miles north on the Licking. Kincaid Lake State Park covers 850 acres and is known for largemouth bass. Planning and Zoning administers floodplain rules, so a house near the Licking deserves a flood zone check before it goes on the market. Public schools are Pendleton County High School north of Falmouth, Sharp Middle School, Northern Elementary in Butler and Southern Elementary in Falmouth. The Kentucky Wool Festival and the Kincaid Regional Theatre are part of local life.

sections.h2: What does the Census say about housing in Pendleton County?
sections.html:
Seller expectations should follow local numbers. The Census Bureau's QuickFacts table lists these for Pendleton County:

  • 14,800 residents in July 2025, about 1.1% above the April 2020 base.
  • 6,341 housing units, with 74.7% of homes owner-occupied.
  • A median owner-occupied value of $159,800 and median gross rent of $793.
  • Median owner costs of $1,172 with a mortgage and $475 without one.
  • Median household income of $64,669 and a mean commute of 36.4 minutes.

The 2020 census counted 6,263 housing units, 11.7% of them vacant, in a county where every resident lives in a rural area. The Census Bureau recorded zero building permits for 2025. Homes in Pendleton County therefore tend to be older, owner-held properties, and an inherited house or a place needing repairs is a common reason for a quick sale.

faqs.q: When did Pendleton County mail its 2026 tax bills?
faqs.a: September 30, 2026. The sheriff asks owners without a bill by October 12 to phone 859-654-4511.

faqs.q: How large is the late charge after January in Pendleton County?
faqs.a: It is 21% for February 1 through April 15, 2027. Payments during January 2027 carry a 5% penalty.

faqs.q: Where can a deed be recorded in Pendleton County?
faqs.a: At the County Clerk's office, Room 1 at 233 Main Street, Falmouth. It opens weekdays from 8:30 to 4:00 and on the second and last Saturday of the month from 8:30 to noon.

faqs.q: Does the buyer or the seller pay the Kentucky transfer tax in Pendleton County?
faqs.a: The seller does, because the tax is charged to the grantor. On the $159,800 Census median value it comes to $160.00.

faqs.q: Must I see the PVA before appealing a Pendleton County assessment?
faqs.a: Yes. A conference with the PVA or a deputy comes first, and the appeal is then filed with the county clerk by the workday after the inspection period closes.
